x: Bailey, of Salford, was leading, followed by Holden (Tipton H.), Evenson (Salford H.), Webster (Birchfield H.), Dodd (Wirrall A.C.), Sutherland (Birchfield H.) and —yes! a Belgrave vest—Penny, seventh.

More by luck that judgment I was well placed in the seventh position, at the end of the first mile, with Bailey (Salford), Holden (Tipton), Evenson (Salford), Webster (Birchfield), Dodd (Wirral A.C.) and Sutherland (Birchfield) in front of me.

At four miles Burns (Elswick) was in the lead, followed by Sutherland (Birchfield), Holden (Tipton), Eaton (Salford), Dodd (Wirral), Robinson (Birchfield), Penny (Belgrave) and Weatherill (S.L.H.) Birchfield were said to have six men in 19 at this point, and we looked certain of a place.

I immediately sensed Sam Dodd was stone cold, and felt sure he would not be where he ought to be at the finish. Billy Eaton told me as he passed, "Can't breathe"; perhaps caused by the extremely hot atmosphere, or maybe tight jersey; the latter a point upon which we shall have to "do something," as…
We trust that Dodd's studies will be followed by a London appointment, and that we may have his services for many years to come.
Dodd, representing the Northern Counties A.A., win the Pole Vault. Dodd hopes to be back again with us shortly, following on his studies in the North, and we shall have a welcome for him.
(3) Frank Kemp and John Key each set Junior records while still youths. (4) Only two pre-war records remain on the books - Dodd's high-jump and Harry Churcher's 2 mile walk.

At seven miles Burns (Elswick) had increased his lead to one of over 100 yards from Holden (Tipton) and Dodd (Wirral), who were together. Penny had shaken off some of his opposition and was now sixth.
This without two of our best men, Pack 4th in the 440 yards and Dodd winning the pole vault who were tied representing others on that occasion.
